newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open firmer, expecting rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open firmer, expecting rate cut.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Friday as a higher than expected unemployment rate prompted forecasts of a bank rate cut today, dealers said.
"The market's discounted a cut, waiting for 9 o'clock (0900 EDT)," said a Toronto-based T-bill trader. The Bank of Canada is seen dropping the bank rate to 3.75 percent from 4.0 percent.
He said the call loan rate was trading at 3.55 percent, almost at the bottom of the Bank of Canada's 3.50-4.0 percent target range.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.33 percent from 3.40 percent at Thursday's close of trading.
But the short-term money market weakened after the Bank of Canada did not cut short-term interest rates as of 0900 EDT/1300 GMT.
The dollar opened softer on Friday at C$1.3538 (US$0.7387) from Thursday's close of C$1.3503 (US$0.7406) after touching a year high earlier this week.

Market players were spooked by a surprisingly high unemployment rate for September -- 9.9 percent versus month earlier 9.4 percent. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the rate would slip to 9.3 percent.
"They're (the Bank of Canada) a little concerned with the currency weakening with the unemployment data," one trader said. "They're holding."
He added that Canada's central bank was still seen cutting rates at a later date.
In mid-morning trading, call loan slipped to 3.60-3.70 percent, closer to the middle of the Bank of Canada's range.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued bill strengthened to 3.57 percent from Thursday's close of 3.65 percent. The one-year when-issued bill firmed to yield 3.79 percent from 3.85 percent.
